It is completely understandable to feel hurt and confused by an abrupt end to therapy. Ethically, therapists are required to avoid client abandonment, which is why providing referrals is a necessary step when ending treatment. A therapist might need to terminate if they experience severe countertransference or an unmanageable rupture with legal guardians, as these issues can prevent them from providing effective care. In such cases, stepping down is often considered the ethical choice to protect the client.

However, abruptly terminating without any explanation is generally discouraged by professional guidelines. While therapists have the right to end treatment if they cannot provide adequate care, best practices dictate that they should communicate the reasons clearly and offer a proper termination process to minimize harm. If you are feeling left in the dark, it may be helpful to discuss this experience with a new therapist who can help you process this difficult transition and provide the stable support you deserve.
